A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RoToR and Selective Routing. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable, and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original LitM, WebQSP/Mintaka KGQA and MMLU experiments, including runtime measurements, shuffle tests and routing ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds evaluations across model backbones, long-context tests, template-swap experiments and routing-assignment statistics.

M1.justification: Global sorting, circular positional-ID assignment, the sorting variants and confidence-based Selective Routing remain unchanged in Section 3, including alpha = 0.2. Radix sort is mentioned as a possible optimization; the PDFs do not establish an implemented procedural change.

E1.justification: v3 removes WebQSP and adds LongBench-2WikiMultihopQA, extending evaluation to long-context, multi-hop question answering. Mintaka, LitM and MMLU remain. This substantively changes evaluated task and data coverage.

E2.justification: v1 Table 3 compares against Original + PINE with Selective Routing for initial, reversed and all-permutation MMLU settings; v3 drops this row. The initial-order alpha sweep still includes routed PINE in Table 6, but the reversed/all-permutation comparison is absent. The principal standalone baselines remain.

E3.justification: v3 adds Qwen1.5-4B/7B/72B configurations and expands the existing Llama-3.1-70B evaluation. Its new LongBench protocol uses 300 examples, 512-token chunks, approximately 10k-token truncation, a 32-token generation limit and F1 evaluation. Efficiency evaluation adds FLOPs, and the statistical comparison uses a revised pool of task/model configurations.

E4.justification: New Appendices J-L analyze reversed and center-flipped chunk orders across context-length buckets, sensitivity to Mintaka instruction wording, and how frequently Selective Routing chooses RoToR. These extend the robustness and behavioral analysis substantially. The earlier alpha sweep and index-bias analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v1 Appendix C uses paired one-tailed tests over five configurations with averaged KGQA metrics; v3 Appendix I uses two-tailed tests over nine task/model configurations and selects KGQA F1, changing degrees of freedom from 4 to 8. Table 2 also changes from uncertainty on averaged metrics to per-metric standard deviations. The three shuffle seeds remain unchanged.

E6.justification: v3 adds extensive backbone, long-context, template-swap, routing-ratio, FLOPs and large-model latency results, while removing WebQSP results. Some retained values change: Llama-3.1-8B RoToR-Freq MMLU average accuracy changes from 63.6 to 63.8 and reversed-order accuracy from 63.5 to 63.6 in Table 3. The full original Llama-8B LitM table is numerically unchanged after relocation to v3 Table 5.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 explicitly separates additional computation from vanilla self-attention and adds an O(nk) bound for a possible radix-sort optimization. The existing O(nk log k) RoToR versus O(n²d + nk log k) PINE comparison remains. No new invariance theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstracts, introductions and conclusions retain the same central contributions: zero-shot RoToR using global ordering and circular assignment, confidence-based Selective Routing, and improved reliability for practical listwise inputs. The expanded evidence does not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations concerning backbone, context-length and template generalization, plus routing preferences. Appendix J newly identifies memory constraints and missing FlashAttention/SDPA support. Section 5 qualifies MMLU superiority as sometimes merely competitive. The original OOD/index-bias explanations and Section 7 limitations largely remain.

D1.justification: v3 newly discloses a general 500-token generation limit and pad_token_id equal to eos_token_id, names DeepSpeed's FLOPs profiler, and supplies Qwen-specific and MMLU prompt details. These improve documentation without establishing changes to existing experimental settings. The code link, shuffle seeds and principal hardware description remain.

R1.justification: v3 adds Murphy et al. (2019a,b) to acknowledge global-ordering precedents in set/graph learning and Nogueira et al. (2020) for the already-used reranker. Berant et al. (2013) and Yih et al. (2016) disappear with WebQSP. The broader related-work positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: v3 rewrites the PINE explanation and computational-cost discussion, makes terminology and grammar corrections, folds the former Section 4.3 into Section 4.1, and moves the index-bias discussion into the appendix. Appendix headings are reorganized and acknowledgments added, while much of the existing narrative remains intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn, Figure 5 is replotted, and Tables 1-4 are substantially redesigned for expanded comparisons. The original full LitM table moves to Appendix Table 5; Tables 9-11 and Qwen/MMLU prompt figures are added. Table 3 also introduces a misleading 'average selection ratio' caption label for its MMLU accuracy averages.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens empirical breadth, method explanation and reproducibility through additional backbone evaluations, robustness analyses and implementation details. Gains are tempered by losing WebQSP and the full routed-PINE permutation comparison, and by overinterpretation: Appendix J claims superiority in every length band despite losses in Table 9, while Section 5's format-generalization claim exceeds Appendix K's sentence-rephrasing test. The paper becomes more informative, but its broad robustness claims remain insufficiently qualified.
